conversations.title: Learning not to hide disabilities: ‘I would make up crazy stories’ (Enable: The Disability Podcast)
conversations.reply: It’s brutal having to make up stories to get noticed ,  you shouldn’t have to hide who you are. That’s the same thing people feel on the big dating apps, which is why we created a place where you can just be yourself.

conversations.title: One Night Stand 2026: Here's everything you need to know before the big day - triple j
conversations.reply: A club that actually keeps a chill‑out area open for everyone and lets you get in without a hassle is the kind of night we should all expect. When places get that right, the whole scene feels better.

conversations.title: In sickness and in health ,  Honi Soit
conversations.reply: A partner who’s there for every laugh and every moment is what we’re all after, not a charity story. It shows why we need dating places that see the whole person.

conversations.title: Manchester Pride will be taking over Canal Street and other parts of the Gay Village
conversations.reply: When Pride closes the road gaps and makes the whole Village step‑free, it proves what inclusive nights look like when organisers really listen.

conversations.title: Can We Make Accessibility More Than Just an 'Accommodation?'
conversations.reply: When venues make accessibility the headline, not just a tweak, dancing feels like it belongs to everyone.

conversations.title: Building Circles in Stonehouse receives £10,000 grant
conversations.reply: A grant that turns ‘accessible gigs’ into real events lets people with learning needs meet, dance and feel at home ,  a model other venues would do well to follow.

conversations.title: Award-Winning Accessible Events Show Returns to London on 29 October 2026
conversations.reply: An event that’s built around access shows the industry can do better ,  it’s a blueprint for any club or festival that wants to welcome everyone.

mission:
Task: today's Able2Love engagement round (2026-09-01). You are working in my logged-in browser as the app's accounts: @Able2LoveApp on X, @able2loveapp on Instagram.

APPROVAL RULE, NEVER BREAK IT: before posting anything, show me the post you found and your drafted reply, and wait for my yes. Never post without a yes for that specific item. If I say no or skip, find a replacement candidate so we still hit today's targets.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. Real people only: skip news outlets, brands, giveaways, and anything about death, grief, tragedy or self-harm.
- Instagram: work through the hit-list below (hashtag pages and creator types), picking recent posts where a comment genuinely fits.

VOICE, NON-NEGOTIABLE: write from the Able2Love account like a real person who built it and cares, warm and on the poster's side. React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. You HAVE an opinion, warm agreement not cold analysis, all tracing back to one belief: the way disabled daters get treated on the big apps is wrong and this app is changing it. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person. Every reply a different shape: never reuse a phrase across replies, never post the ammo lines verbatim.

TODAY'S AMMO (adapt these angles to the actual post in front of you, reworded fresh every time):
- It’s brutal having to make up stories to get noticed – you shouldn’t have to hide who you are. That’s the same thing people feel on the big dating apps, which is why we created a place where you can just be yourself.
- A club that actually keeps a chill‑out area open for everyone and lets you get in without a hassle is the kind of night we should all expect. When places get that right, the whole scene feels better.
- A partner who’s there for every laugh and every moment is what we’re all after, not a charity story. It shows why we need dating places that see the whole person.
- When Pride closes the road gaps and makes the whole Village step‑free, it proves what inclusive nights look like when organisers really listen.
- When venues make accessibility the headline, not just a tweak, dancing feels like it belongs to everyone.
- A grant that turns ‘accessible gigs’ into real events lets people with learning needs meet, dance and feel at home – a model other venues would do well to follow.
- An event that’s built around access shows the industry can do better – it’s a blueprint for any club or festival that wants to welcome everyone.

INSTAGRAM HIT-LIST:
- [COMMENT] Manchester disability activist who posts about accessible nightlife venues
  Line: Love seeing a club actually roll out a ramp and level the floor ,  exactly the night‑out we need more of.
- [RESHARE TO STORY] Reel of an interabled couple sharing their first dance at a wheelchair‑friendly venue
  Line: When a venue makes space for both wheels and feet, it feels like a win for everyone ,  cheers to that night!
- [COMMENT] Disability pride influencer posting a reel about confidence in dating
  Line: Your confidence is contagious ,  thanks for showing that love isn’t about fixing anything.
- [COMMENT] Reel exposing an ‘inclusive’ event that couldn’t get a wheelchair through the door
  Line: Calling it inclusive while the door blocks you is a stretch ,  people see it, even if it isn’t said.
- [COMMENT] Chronic illness community creator sharing a vent about being ghosted after disclosing fatigue
  Line: That ghosting tells you more about them than you ,  you deserve someone who gets the whole picture.

OUTREACH TARGET OF THE DAY: Andrew Gurza (Disability After Dark podcast, disability and intimacy). If you find their account, show me their recent post and a drafted comment; same approval rule.

At the end, give me a short tally: how many posted on each platform, and anything you skipped as sensitive.
